The mass-point count near the cutoff decides the discreteness route: with few mass points the continuity density test is NOT_APPLICABLE and the binomial test plus in-window balance replaces it; with many, rddensity with mass-point adjustment is run.

Covariate and placebo-outcome balance is tested through the headline procedure at each variable's own data-driven bandwidth, plus at the headline bandwidth as a labelled supplement; imbalance with a continuous density is reported as design-validity evidence.
Placebo cutoffs use only one side's observations with the bandwidth reselected at each cutoff; a placebo pooling across the true cutoff is redone.
Donut checks run in every RD at several radii with the bandwidth reselected and per-side counts reported.
RD plots are re-drawn with data-driven bins and the local fit inside the estimation window; a jump only under the paper's bins or only in a global polynomial is a presentation finding.

A covariate-adjusted RD headline is checked against the unadjusted benchmark: predetermined balanced additive covariates, bandwidth reselected with them, and any shift decomposed into bandwidth and adjustment parts.
Fuzzy RD: first stage first with F >= 20 or the claim falls back to ITT; single-bandwidth ratio with RBC; falsification on assignment; the estimand is the complier effect at the cutoff.

Regression kink designs get a policy-rule audit, slope-change density and covariate tests, an order x selector grid with RBC intervals, and a placebo-kink permutation test of the paper's exact estimator.

Boundary designs: classify the pooled border specification; density-type WBATE as the comparison for the pooled estimate; claims about location judged on the uniform band; distance-based estimates near border kinks refit location-based; compound-treatment overlay; point-by-point covariate balance.

Multiple cutoffs: report pooling weights and cutoff-specific estimates; classify cumulative vs non-cumulative; cross-cutoff tests use bias-corrected estimates and robust variances; per-cutoff falsification.
A claim about RD effects away from the cutoff is graded unsupported unless the paper names and defends an extrapolation assumption.
Heterogeneous RD effects need RBC intervals per subgroup and an RBC test of the difference; the heterogeneity variable is tested for a jump at the cutoff.
RD power or MDE is computed at the paper's own specification against an effect fixed outside the data, never the paper's estimate.
Clustered RD inference: compare SEs at fixed h and b, state the vce, and route fewer than about 10 clusters per side inside the window to small-n-diagnostics.
Backing out an unstated bandwidth is done per side after establishing which N is printed, sweeping vce, covariates, regularization, fuzzy target and package version as well as selectors.

Regression-kink and RD-extrapolation records added; local-randomization record gains estimand labels, window-selection settings, binomial test and nested-window sensitivity; boundary record gains specification class, kinks, compound treatment and density-type weights.

RD code examples run on current rdpackages releases: summary(all=TRUE) for three rows in rdrobust >= 4.0.0, explicit CR1 for clustered fits, rdrandinf ci= for intervals, rdms with distinct cutoffs, rdhte_contrast for differences, rdplot local fit.
check_inference.py skips report files that HANDOFF.md lists under ## excluded (not evidence); every input and stage report is still checked.

VtF must be computed on jackknife inputs (jackknife covariance of reduced-form and first-stage coefficients) in few/unequal-cluster or shift-share designs; vtf.ado (CR1/HC1 only) is a tagged companion row. check_inference.py F6 (untagged vtf call) and F7 (IV report without a jackknife VtF set). Crib no longer calls jackknife inputs an implementation choice.

Delete-one-shock jackknife defined: control the deleted shock's share at unit level and re-fit everything (MNW 2023 eq. 15; BHJ 2022 Prop. 5); shock-level row deletion with controls partialled once is invalid; validation that the leave-top-shock-out estimate equals the share-controlled unit regression is required.

Null-imposed Anderson-Rubin sets in few/unequal-cluster or shift-share designs are inverted by grid search on y - b0*endog tested at zero; boottest ..., ar (unrestricted bootstrap DGP) fails check_inference.py F8 unless tagged AR-boottest-robustness; iv-diagnostics reports must state the Montiel Olea-Pflueger effective F (F13; fallback via e(cmdline) fix, residualisation, or MOP eq. 3 when weakivtest refuses ivreghdfe; never Cragg-Donald under clustering).

Stata boottest with jk must specify noci (check_inference.py F9: boottest prints a default confidence set whose jk inversion is invalid at non-zero nulls), and every Stata boottest call must be followed by assert !missing(r(p)) (F10: refused models exit with rc 0 and missing r(p)); hand-coded CV3 loops must re-estimate non-cluster FEs inside each leave-out.

HonestDiD after csdid or R did::att_gt requires a universal base period (csdid ..., long2, never default varying base or long; base_period = "universal" in att_gt) and positive e(b) vector positions in Stata honestdid pre()/post(), enforced by check_inference.py F11.

Local-randomization RD confidence intervals (rdrandinf ci() / rdsensitivity tlist()) must be checked against min(grid) and max(grid) so narrow grids do not silently truncate the interval at the grid boundaries.

R urca::ur.df on cointegration residuals prints raw unit-root critical values (niv = 1) and must be evaluated against urca:::.urcval MacKinnon response-surface critical values with niv = m; Stata scpc requires robust/cluster() on the preceding fit (to populate e(V_modelbased)) and the spur LBM-GLS transformed model when raw OLS with many controls aborts.

check_inference.py F4 requires the randomization (permutation) p of the actual statistic inside the Placebo-shock rejection rates section, and F12 requires a shock-level jackknife (CV3) row in every shift-share report.

Non-linear estimators (L1/median regression, quantile regression, logit, Poisson) cannot use OLS FWL pre-partialling of non-cluster fixed effects in a CV3 leave-one-cluster-out loop; include the non-cluster FEs directly inside each leave-out refit.

In a regression kink design, test covariate slope continuity with rdrobust(..., deriv = 1) on each predetermined covariate and density slope continuity with rddensity(..., p = 2) (and p = 1 for level continuity).

check_spec_drift.py filters out review-digest and audit-review scope rows when checking a review run's spec drift; check_coverage.py excludes files listed under ## excluded in HANDOFF.md from resolving coverage obligations and checks report deferral prose before coverage-na.csv; resolved ERRATA.md items are marked status: closed by the audit.

check_facts.py accepts derived numbers (differences, ratios) not literally present in the corpus when their line is ruled in ISSUES.facts.md, and excludes files listed under ## excluded in HANDOFF.manifest.json even inside an accepted directory; render_digest.py --stale-check allows INTERIM handoff status on preview digests.

Fire whimsical-assumptions-diagnostics for any load-bearing conclusion or prescription derived from a model: inventory stated, structural, closure, exclusion and bridge premises; relax each in a realistic direction and run it; grade its warrant from sources; rule WHIMSICAL only when critical and unwarranted are both shown; write assumption-ledger.csv and the module report.

check_manifest.py check 10: assumption-ledger.csv is required when the module walk fires whimsical-assumptions-diagnostics; enums, grounding, artifacts for every tested effect, sources for every graded warrant, and both legs on WHIMSICAL rows are enforced.

After the first test run: decide value-vs-premise before building (value disputes go to quantitative-model-diagnostics); a relaxation lists every change, is sized from a same-quantity source or reported as a flip threshold, stays model-consistent, and uses the intermediate case before the pole; effects quote the conclusion they move and count only against it; bound crossings are one bound-check finding (not demonstrated, not false); BUILT_IN excludes valid theorems; companion estimates count only at their review verdict; web sources are saved into the job tree; defender constructions are part of the record; judge rules for kept caveats, multi-conclusion rows, merges and out-of-scope routing.

After the second test run: check the paper's robustness tables before building; effects in the conclusion's units (a unit switch is a second change); no unsized central cases; a source's model section is not evidence; new margins reported as thresholds; effect NO_COUNTERPART; direction judged per conclusion; about-X tolerance set by the paper's range or rounding; each load-bearing conclusion ruled and the row takes the most severe; ruling CONSUMED for sister-module findings; DISCARDED and CONSUMED name where they were routed (enforced by check_manifest.py); defender regressions remove legs only; fragile UNRESOLVED rows reported beside the findings; inventory assigns no legs.

Ruling FRAGILE (unwarranted; conclusion breaks only beyond a threshold no source reaches) with effect THRESHOLD, reported beside WHIMSICAL findings; sign-deciding assumed values take THRESHOLD; a model-data match whose model side is an identity of an input is BUILT_IN; every role saves web sources; the judge checks script settings against logs; a paper robustness table is cited from a saved page extract. check_manifest.py enforces FRAGILE = THRESHOLD + unwarranted.

About-X tolerance includes a sensitivity table the paper cites in support of X; a fraction in words covers half the step to its neighbours; CONTESTED supports FRAGILE only when no source places the margin on the safe side of the threshold; a zero-width threshold goes to the bound check; CONSUMED covers findings already confirmed by another module or stage, including code-and-data defects.

Every report, SYNTHESIS.md, CHANGELOG.md open/operator item, and message to the operator names the substance in words first — never a bare section number (§7.3, the §3.6 results, §6, §4a), a review-internal or crib section, or a bare claim/finding ID (CL08, C14) as a noun; a section number or ID may follow in parentheses after the thing is named.

Rendered prose in ISSUES.md names paper sections by their substance (a section number may follow in parentheses as a locator, never stand in as the noun) and never renders review-internal section references; check_style.py flags unparenthesized § locators and review-internal § references on rendered lines.

Any file found during acquisition that may hold the paper's own observations or results in another form (author or co-author site, OSF, Dataverse, a later pooled/meta-analysis/replication file) is saved under lit/data/ with URL, date and hash and listed, whatever the finding worker's brief — never discarded unread or deleted; the data audit matches every such second record to the deposit row by row, diffs matched cells, lists unmatched rows, and re-runs the headline tests on each version.

Five stages: paper, code-and-data, claims, challenge, verdict. The stress stage, its re-derivations and the third-agent adjudication are removed; review/challenge-REPORT*.md and work/challenge/ replace review/stress-REPORT.md and work/stress/.

The claim ledger is a truth ledger with no severity: each load-bearing claim records centrality (headline, supporting, peripheral), holds (holds, narrower, not established), kernel, what is not established, the strongest defence (tested?) and status.

An untestable defence shields nothing when it rests on materials the authors did not deposit or on a printed statement the deposited data contradict; the row is decided on the evidence that exists. A testable, untested defence makes the row INTERIM.

Where a finding removes support for an attribution the paper makes in some of its samples, the claims resting on those samples are not established for that attribution, even where other samples still carry the headline.

Run the challenge stage before any verdict: a fresh agent on the verdict-routed model tests every claim-ledger row, every stage and module finding and every review-built calculation, in both directions; rebuilds from the pristine deposit and the printed page, never running the review's scripts; rules STANDS, STANDS WITH CHANGES, WRONG or ADD on evidence only, with no severity; findings it did not rebuild stand; a worker re-runs the load-bearing script before a WRONG or STANDS WITH CHANGES ruling is relied on. Without it the run is INTERIM.

Test for findings filed where they do least and for rescues carrying the same defect; apply the inference traps (moved from the audit's inference check); for each review-built calculation, write its requirements from the paper and code before reading the review's version, rebuild it and mark each met or failed (moved from the audit's construction reader).

The challenge report carries sections (a) ruling per claim without severity, (b) element table with direction, (c) strongest case each way, (d) not rebuilt, (e) adverse results, (f) not tested, (g) counts of rulings by direction and of calculation requirements met and failed.

One fresh agent writes SYNTHESIS.md: header counts by holds; Status; What the paper establishes and what it does not, led by the finding that removes or narrows most headline claims; design-level findings with a bears-on line; the final claim ledger (Centrality, Holds, Kernel, Not established, Strongest defence, Status); estimator table; data integrity (a printed statement of method the data contradict is a verified error; name the tests run); findings ordered by centrality then holds; counts of moved rows and challenge rulings by direction, a one-sided count justified. No severity. It may set aside a challenge ruling only after its script is re-run; nothing re-decides after it.
A print/prose/code mismatch counts against a claim only once its effect on the printed cell has been run, where the code runs.
Stage-report finding blocks carry a bears-on line naming the claims they touch, not a severity.

The audit is mechanical: completeness, re-run, print check, row check, propagation, traceability. The inference check, the construction reader and VALIDATION.md, the verdict judge and the separate editor are removed; the audit rates no claim.

A correction that changes what a finding says, or touches a number, quote or page a claim-ledger row, design-level finding or the bottom line rests on, is marked → VERDICT; after the mechanical items are applied the review's verdict stage runs once, fresh, on the corrected reports. No row goes back through the challenge stage.

Completeness requires challenge reports covering every claim-ledger row, stage finding and review-built calculation with their counts, and a verdict-stage SYNTHESIS.md with every required section. A v0.6.2–v0.7.x run: read stress reports as challenge reports ignoring their ratings, add centrality and holds to the ledger, list re-derivations, adjudications and stress checks as superseded, and run the verdict stage fresh.

The residue and bare-ID sweep covers reader-facing files only (SYNTHESIS.md, CHANGELOG.md open items, messages to the operator). The SYNTHESIS header carries the Replication word and the verdict stage's holds counts.
Back up the job tree with a commit before applying corrections, never with file or tree copies; build HANDOFF.md once, after all corrections land.

Severity is assigned by the digest as a reading aid: each issue's default is the most severe default among its mapped claim rows (not established: High for headline and supporting, Medium for peripheral; narrower: Medium for headline and supporting, Low for peripheral); a departure needs a severity-reason field (internal, never rendered); the coverage gate lists departures and FAILs one without a reason; the fairness and prose passes never change a severity.

Coverage obligations are claim rows that do not hold, design-level findings and finding blocks; a headline or supporting row that does not hold may not go to caveats, avenues or exclusion except as a superseded twin. Legacy Severity tables are still read.

Issue ranking follows the truth ledger: headline before supporting before peripheral, not established before narrower, then number of claims, with the bottom-line finding first. The bottom-line check compares Summary and Assessment with SYNTHESIS's What the paper establishes section and allows nothing softer.
No rewrite clears the paper beyond what upstream established: integrity sentences name the tests run, and 'not shown to change' is never written as 'does not change'.
ISSUES.md front-matter verdict records the Replication word and the holds counts (internal, never rendered).
Judgement routing: stage and module reports, the claim ledger, the challenge stage and the verdict stage go to the verdict model; audit-review tasks are mechanical apart from a routed verdict re-run.

A sentence the paper itself presents as conjecture or hypothesis, and does not elsewhere state or use as a finding, claims only plausibility: record it holds unless evidence contradicts it, with a kernel saying it is untested; the same proposition stated as established elsewhere is its own row; a hedge in wording only does not count.

Only a correction that could change a claim-ledger row's holds or kernel, a design-level finding or the bottom line is → VERDICT; locators, verbatim quotes, numbers restated to their logs and miscounts that leave a finding's conclusion unchanged are TEXT, applied directly, including in a synthesis the verdict stage has just rewritten.

A corrected row goes straight to the verdict stage, never back through the challenge stage; a row the completeness check adds is written by the claims stage and tested once by the challenge stage before the verdict re-run.

The coverage walk skips a job's copy of the skill tree (_skill/) and its bulk scratch (_bulk/); a claim row several issues carry is ruled → issues N, M and sets each issue's default; design-level findings set no default themselves, their rows are mapped directly; the Summary's headline list is the headline rows.

Coverage gate: an issue mapped to no truth-ledger row defaults to Low and its departures need a reason (runs before v0.8 have no defaults); SYNTHESIS's truth table is read in place of the generated claim-ledger CSV's truth rows; every target of a multi-issue ruling must overlap the finding; block findings are read from their heading and first five lines. A rung (3)+ integrity finding is rated High with that as its reason.
The claim-ledger table keeps the claims stage's row order, and each claim cell ends with its page and row ID in parentheses, where later scripts read the ID.
TEXT items in SYNTHESIS.md are applied after a verdict re-run, other TEXT items before; an errata round amends HANDOFF.md and rebuilds the manifest.

Issue ranking follows the logic of the case: the issue carrying the bottom line's lead finding first, then each issue before the issues that rest on it, otherwise the paper's order of claims; severity tags need not descend with rank. Supersedes the truth-ledger tier ranking.

Coverage rulings to an issue carry the issue's title words (→ issue N ("title words")); in a truth-ledger run an unbound ruling FAILs and a title the issue no longer has FAILs; the claims stage's provisional tables are ignored when SYNTHESIS has the truth table; a phrase that decides several findings is listed as ambiguous.

The fact sweep resolves quotes against primary sources only: every review report (including grouped *-REPORT-*.md), review/*.md, PROGRESS.md, AGENTS.md, 00_INTAKE.md and the job's skill copy are excluded; _skill/ and _bulk/ are not walked.

A verdict re-run routed by audit-review is scoped: it re-decides what the → VERDICT corrections bear on, carries every other row and finding over with its label, grouping and wording, and lists any other change with its evidence under 'Changed outside the routed corrections'; the audit runs it unscoped only when its completeness check added stages or claim rows.

The audit's checklist is the review skill at the run's recorded suite version: the current skill for a run in use, the run's own tagged snapshot for a run frozen for a corpus or release test (upgraded only on the operator's request); a verdict re-run that cannot start in a fresh context leaves the audit INTERIM.
A contested coverage ruling FAILs unless ERRATA.md holds an open, finding-bearing FOR-AUDIT-REVIEW item quoting the contested finding.
Where the attacker, defender and judge roles run as separate passes in one context rather than separate agents, the module report says so (likewise the whimsical-assumptions roles).

python3 in every command means a Python 3.10+ interpreter with the README's packages; a subagent the harness bars from writing files returns its report text and the coordinator saves it unchanged; rule 6 covers a defect in shipped data (the variant changes only the defective cells and saves the data diff as its patch).

A not-applicable module report carries 'Status: NOT_APPLICABLE — <reason>' and owes no module lines; a fired module may not be a stub. Fired modules run as separate agents write their own reports, append rows to results.csv and battery-manifest.csv under a lock in the stage's column order, and put leads in their own Leads section for the stage agent to fold in; a stage builder never regenerates a shared ledger once modules have appended; module scripts and logs follow the stage's paths.

A completed robustness-claim scan with no hits is one row classified NONE_FOUND with the search stems as evidence (a header-only file WARNs); robustness columns are snake_case; findings sit under the three group labels, most important first within each, the gravest named in Status.

assets/claim-ledger.csv is the ledger template; one sentence may become several rows when its claim holds at one inference level and has no valid test at another; the claim-test matrix sits in claims-REPORT.md; driver-matrix.csv gains data_version and transform.

Requirements for a review-built calculation are written before opening the review's scripts and logs for it; the challenge sorts a one-column evidence field into both directions, gives each element the direction its content cuts, and counts claim-row rulings on their own line; a challenge agent barred from writing returns its report text.

Re-grading a row on the claims-stage definitions while keeping the challenge's evidence is not setting a ruling aside; designs with no instrument write 'not applicable (no instrument)' in the first-stage columns and may record a magnitude 'not measured' on confounding grounds; findings rank by the highest-ranked claim they bear on, ties in the paper's order, findings on holding rows after, limits on the review in their own list; an untested claim is holds 'not established', status 'untested'; a scoped re-run records 'Re-decided on the routed corrections' before 'Changed outside the routed corrections'.

A job folder with no repository is initialised (local) before the first commit; re-runs happen in place after a commit, but a script that appends to a shared ledger is re-run in a copy or rebuilt from its builder; every TEXT item, SYNTHESIS.md included, goes in before a scoped verdict re-run; errata routed back are classified by the audit's own TEXT/→ VERDICT test; a verbatim quotation of tested evidence is exempt from instance hunts; the residue sweep exempts the verdict's Counts record; untagged display equations are checked by hand; errata close with a resolution: line.

finding-bearing means the item could change a claim row's holds or kernel, a design-level finding or the bottom line; a slip that leaves a conclusion unchanged is routed but does not block. Integrity sentences state what the integrity evidence covers, never a list of checks. Staleness is judged by the manifest's hashes (mtime a hint). The fresh coverage pass writes the dispositions; a row maps to the issues carrying its stated reason; fresh gate records live under work/digest/; deposit files and files the paper names may render; FAIRNESS.md and ISSUES.keeps.md are always written under a manual pass; the apparatus list is stated and matches corpus_rules.py.

Gates: every script runs under python -I; the style gate's manual pass catches 'FAIL L<n>' lines; the fact sweep flags a ledger number more precise than its source (precision upgrade), excludes work/digest/ from its corpora, and skips the References section's numbers.

The stage's gates run once the fired modules have reported (missing module reports before then are expected, the stage INTERIM); a review-built calculation is unvalidated until it has its patch and moments file, then clean, and invalid if the challenge's rebuild fails one of its requirements; 'the operator's routing' is defined (whatever the operator or harness sets, else the session's model).
ai-sweep moves inside review-digest (review-digest/ai-sweep/); the prose gate finds its engine at ai-sweep/scripts within the digest skill, and the sweep can still be linked in as a skill of its own.
